concepts.explanation: Software calls the state 0 or 1, but the machine still needs a physical difference it can measure. In electronics that difference is usually voltage, current, charge, or a radio signal state.
concepts.firstPrinciples: A bit is information represented by a distinguishable physical state.
concepts.title: Bits

concepts.explanation: A byte is not automatically meaningful. It becomes meaningful only when a protocol or schema says how to interpret the bit pattern.
concepts.firstPrinciples: A byte is eight bits, which gives 256 possible patterns.
concepts.title: Bytes

concepts.explanation: Two devices can receive the same bit pattern and still disagree unless they share rules for packet shape, timing, roles, fields, and meaning.
concepts.firstPrinciples: A protocol is a rulebook for interpreting and exchanging bit patterns.
concepts.title: Protocol

concepts.explanation: The PHY layer does not know what a sensor value means. It makes the radio transmission possible and turns radio energy into bits that higher layers can use.
concepts.firstPrinciples: The PHY layer handles the physical radio path between signal and bits.
concepts.title: PHY Layer

concepts.explanation: It decides when packets are exchanged, whether a device is advertising or connected, and how connection events are maintained. It is below the app-level meaning of the data.
concepts.firstPrinciples: The Link Layer controls radio packet exchange and connection mechanics.
concepts.title: Link Layer

concepts.explanation: GAP is how BLE devices become discoverable and decide who connects to whom. It is not the place where your sensor payload's fields are defined.
concepts.firstPrinciples: GAP defines device discovery, roles, advertising, and connection setup.
concepts.title: GAP

concepts.explanation: GATT gives the connected devices an application-level structure: services contain characteristics, and characteristics expose values that can be read, written, or notified.
concepts.firstPrinciples: GATT is the connected-data model for services and characteristics.
concepts.title: GATT

concepts.explanation: A characteristic is where a value lives in GATT. Your iPhone can receive a notification from a characteristic, but it still needs your own app logic to parse the bytes.
concepts.firstPrinciples: A characteristic is a named GATT value with allowed operations.
concepts.title: Characteristic

concepts.explanation: Calling notify does not create the sample. It asks the BLE stack to send an already-prepared value through the characteristic to the subscribed central.
concepts.firstPrinciples: A notification sends a characteristic value update to a connected subscriber.
concepts.title: Notifications

gaps.description: Knowing that data is electrical is not enough. A receiver also needs an agreed rulebook for what each bit pattern means.
gaps.title: Physical Signal vs Meaning

gaps.description: Different BLE layers answer different questions: can radio become bits, can packets be exchanged, and what app-level value changed.
gaps.title: BLE Layer Boundaries

gaps.description: Creating data, storing it in a packet, sending a notification, and parsing it on the iPhone are separate steps.
gaps.title: Sample Creation vs Transport

relationships.rationale: A byte is composed of eight bits, so the bit is the physical-information unit inside the byte representation.
The PHY makes radio states distinguishable as bits for higher layers.
Understanding that byte patterns have no inherent meaning is prerequisite to understanding why shared protocol rules are needed.
Link Layer packet exchange depends on the PHY radio path that carries the packet bits.
GAP discovery and connection roles use the advertising and connection mechanics supplied below by the Link Layer.
Devices must discover and establish the appropriate relationship before using the connected GATT data model.
GATT transactions rely on an established BLE connection maintained by lower-layer packet exchange.
A characteristic is a value-bearing element inside the GATT service model.
A notification publishes an update for an existing characteristic value to a subscriber.
A characteristic transports bytes, while a shared payload schema lets the receiving app interpret those bytes consistently.
Notification is a delivery operation; protocol or schema supplies meaning, so neither function should be mistaken for the other.

choices.rationale: Eight is the number of bits in the byte, not the number of distinct patterns those bits can form.
Sixteen would describe four binary positions, not eight.
Each of eight independent binary positions doubles the combinations, giving 2^8 = 256.
1024 is 2^10, so it would require ten binary positions rather than one eight-bit byte.
